news.headline: A Baby Giant Armadillo Caught on Camera!
news.body: Scientists in the Amazon rainforest in Peru set up a hidden camera and filmed something super rare: a baby giant armadillo exploring the forest. Giant armadillos are the biggest armadillos in the world, and they are so hard to spot that some teams wait more than a year to film just one. Local Indigenous experts helped pick the perfect spot. Giant armadillos dig big burrows that lots of other animals use as homes, too!

news.headline: Webb Telescope Spots Weather on a Faraway World
news.body: The James Webb Space Telescope spent 11 hours watching WISE 0855, a "failed star" called a brown dwarf. It is about as big as Jupiter, about 7.5 light-years away, and the coldest one ever found, around 17 degrees Fahrenheit. Scientists saw its water clouds getting thicker and thinner as it spun, a lot like weather on Earth! It is the first time anyone has seen changing water clouds outside our solar system.

news.headline: Tigers, Tuna and Turtles Make a Comeback
news.body: A big new report from the wildlife charity WWF shares some happy news. Wild tigers have almost doubled in about 15 years, from about 3,200 to about 5,700. Bluefin tuna as big as dolphins are leaping off the coast of the UK again after almost disappearing. And green sea turtles are doing so well that they are no longer listed as endangered. Scientists say it shows that helping nature really works.

fun_fact: Nine-banded armadillos almost always have four identical babies at a time. They're born as quadruplets! 🐣

did_you_know: Tigers have striped skin, not just striped fur! Even if a tiger's fur were shaved off, its stripes would still show. 🐅
